A.explanation: A coin has mass of a few grams, about $5 \times 10^{-3}\text{ kg}$, so order $10^{-2}\text{ kg}$ not $10^{-4}\text{ kg}$.

B.explanation: A sheet of paper is about $0.1\text{ mm} = 10^{-4}\text{ m}$ thick, so $10^{-2}\text{ m}$ is 100 times too large.

C.explanation: An apple of mass about $0.1\text{ kg}$ has weight $W = mg$ of about $1\text{ N}$, which is order $10^{0}\text{ N}$.

D.explanation: Body temperature is about $37^{\circ}\text{C} \approx 310\text{ K}$, so order $10^{2}\text{ K}$ not $10^{1}\text{ K}$.

hints: Picture each object in SI units: a coin in $\text{kg}$, paper thickness in $\text{m}$, apple weight from $W = mg$ in $\text{N}$, body temperature in $\text{K}$.
Convert familiar values: a few grams to $\text{kg}$, $0.1\text{ mm}$ to $\text{m}$, and $37^{\circ}\text{C}$ to kelvin by adding 273.
Estimate the apple as about $0.1\text{ kg}$ with $g \approx 10\text{ m s}^{-2}$ and check which power of ten $mg$ is closest to.
walkthrough: Order of magnitude means the nearest power of ten to the typical value in the stated unit, so estimate each quantity in that unit.
Mass of a coin is a few grams, e.g. $5\text{ g} = 5 \times 10^{-3}\text{ kg}$, closest to $10^{-2}\text{ kg}$, not $10^{-4}\text{ kg}$.
Thickness of paper is about $0.1\text{ mm} = 1 \times 10^{-4}\text{ m}$, closest to $10^{-4}\text{ m}$, not $10^{-2}\text{ m}$.
Weight of an apple uses $W = mg$ with $m \approx 0.1\text{ kg}$ and $g \approx 9.81\text{ m s}^{-2}$, giving $W \approx 1\text{ N} = 10^{0}\text{ N}$.
Body temperature is about $37^{\circ}\text{C} = 310\text{ K}$, closest to $10^{2}\text{ K}$, not $10^{1}\text{ K}$, so only the apple row is correct. This is option C.
